text:
morgan: idea — instead of hand-tuned token-buckets for admission to dedicated pools, what about a PID-based feedback loop that nudges admission rate + prewarm signals? can reduce oscillation when tenants spike. sketch below.

kira: curious. how do you prevent instability across many tenants? pid loops per-tenant sounds noisy.

morgan: per-tenant PIDs but with shared dampening and a global safety limiter. PID output -> target admission tokens/sec for tenant. admission controller enforces via leaky-bucket.

raj: prolly need to bound integral term or use anti-windup. also need to handle sudden cold-starts where PID hasn't seen load.

anita: idea: use short-term predictor for request rate (exponential smoothing) to seed PID setpoint on sudden spikes, then let PID stabilize. that handles cold starts.

sam: can we express this as config? like policy below:

sam: ```yaml
policy:
  type: pid_admission
  tenants:
    default:
      kp: 0.8
      ki: 0.03
      kd: 0.1
      integral_limit: 50
      max_tokens_per_sec: 120
  global:
    safety_limit_tokens_per_sec: 2000
    prewarm_on_predictor: true
    predictor:
      method: exp_smooth
      alpha: 0.4
```

kira: nice. need metrics: queue_length, served_tokens/sec, drop_rate, pid_output, predictor_forecast

morgan: agree. plus an SLO guard: if tail_latency > 250ms or error_rate > 0.5% then disable pid and revert to conservative static bucket.

raj: rollout plan? start with one tenant in staging, then canary 5% production, collect stability metrics and fallbacks.

anita: +1. perf cost: more CPU for PID loops + predictor, but negligible compared to GPU. watch control plane resources.

deploy-bot: started canary for pid_admission on pool-gpu-08 (5% traffic) at 2026-03-18T14:32Z

sam: logs from canary: ```json
{"tenant":"team-x","queue_len_avg":6.9,"tokens_served_s":95,"drop_rate":0.012,"pid_out":110}
```

kira: initial look: queue_len stabilized faster, but saw oscillation when two tenants' predictors overshot at same time -> need coordination/higher-level arbiter.

morgan: proposal: add 'coordination window' where global arbiter smooths per-tenant setpoints using moving-average and enforces headroom minimums. will draft RFC.

raj: ok please add failure modes: stuck-integral, predictor bias, network partition; tests needed.

morgan: will draft RFC + smoke tests. thanks all :thumbsup:
